prompt: Your younger sibling confides they have been sneaking out at night to meet friends and makes you promise not to tell. What is the most caring response?

options.text: Promise to keep it secret, because a sibling's trust matters more than anything else
Say you cannot keep a secret about their safety, encourage them to tell a parent or trusted adult with you there for support, and tell an adult yourself if the risk continues
Threaten to tell only when they annoy you, so you can use the secret as leverage
Ignore it and hope it is just a phase that stops on its own

explanation: Sneaking out at night carries real safety risks, so caring means involving a trusted adult even at the cost of short-term trust. Promising secrecy, ignoring it, or using it as leverage leaves your sibling unprotected.
